24990-thirteen-chapters-of-american-hist:
Theodore Sutro's 1905 volume presents Edward Moran's series of thirteen historical marine paintings, each representing a chapter of American history. Sutro dedicates the book to his wife Florence, whose friendship for the Morans led him to champion the series. The paintings run from the earliest exploration to the nation's growth, with text setting each scene in its historical moment.

One chapter shows Henry Hudson entering New York Bay on September 11, 1609. He was an Englishman whom history often misnames Hendrick Hudson, since his ship sailed for the Dutch East India Company from Amsterdam. The book appeared in the year of the Louisiana Purchase Exposition, when America celebrated the centennial of that vast acquisition. It remains a handsome record of history told in paint.
8226-fairy-tales-their-origin-and-meanin:
John Thackray Bunce delivered the substance of this volume as Christmas holiday lectures in 1877 at the Birmingham and Midland Institute, where he was senior vice-president. Finding that subject and matter interested young people, he revised and extended the lectures into a book on fairy tales, their origin and meaning, with some account of dwellers in fairyland. The volume does not pretend to scientific method or complete treatment; its aim is modest, to furnish an inducement rather than a formal introduction to folk lore.

Bunce introduces young readers to the study of folk tales, showing how old stories carry old beliefs. His lectures are clear, curious, and inviting, rather than scholarly. For readers interested in fairy tales and folklore, the book is a charming Victorian starting point, and a record of how the subject first reached a popular audience.
doe-osti-2589397-novel-solar-panel-defec:
National Renewable Energy Laboratory final report NREL/TP-5K00-93973 closes cooperative project CRD-22-22823 with BrightSpot Automation. Technical contact Steven Johnston covers two linked efforts on finding defects in solar panels. One built machine learning software; the other tested a light-based inspection method in the field.

Software work started from a model and labeled cell images supplied by the company. The team tuned competing models, wrote code to run them, and set shared practices for judging their accuracy on electroluminescence images, which reveal cracks and dead areas inside cells. Field work showed ultraviolet fluorescence inspection catching many defect types across panel designs with different service histories. Together the results point to faster, cheaper factory and field checks that feed durability data back to makers.
fairy-tales-their-origin-and-meaning-wit:
Bunce's Fairy Tales, Their Origin and Meaning began as Christmas holiday lectures in 1877. John Thackray Bunce delivered them at the Birmingham and Midland Institute. He was then the institute's senior vice-president. Young hearers liked the subject, so he revised the lectures into a book.

Bunce states a modest aim in his opening note. He wants to tempt readers into folk lore study, not to treat it with full science. He points them to Max Müller and Cox's Mythology of the Aryan Nations. Ralston's Russian Folk Tales and Campbell's West Highlands tales also guide the way. The second half gives some account of dwellers in fairyland. The book suits readers who want a gentle first door into folklore.
podcast-joerogan-3JpWEwfo4Dw:
Joe Rogan turns to the woman who took Marlon Brando's Oscar and the tale of her faked heritage in a segment from his show. Sacheen Littlefeather rose at the 1973 Oscars to refuse the prize for Brando. Late reports said her Native roots were made up.

Rogan works through the night at the Oscars and the row that grew years later. He weighs what the new claims do to her fame and to the cause she spoke for. The segment is short and wry. Listeners get a strange tale of fame and false roots. The library holds the file as an archive record.
